question: Nibbling of uncovered skin with or without bruising or hematoma is classified as what category of rabies exposure?

rationale.text:
Nibbling of uncovered skin with or without bruising or hematoma is classified as Category II. Category of rabies exposure: **Category I** – ·Feeding/touching an animal; ·Licking of intact skin; ·Exposure to a patient with signs and symptoms of rabies by sharing of eating or drinking utensils; ·Casual contact and routine delivery of health care to a patient with signs and symptoms of rabies. **Category II** – ·Nibbling of uncovered skin with or without bruising/hematoma; ·Minor/superficial scratches/abrasions without bleeding, including those induced to bleed; ·All Category II exposures on the head and neck area are considered Category III and shall be managed as such. **Category III** – ·Transdermal bites (puncture wounds, lacerations, avulsions) or scratches/abrasions with spontaneous bleeding; ·Licks on broken skin or mucous membrane; ·Exposure to a rabies patient through bites, contamination of mucous membranes (eyes, oral/nasal mucosa, genital/anal mucous membrane) or open skin lesions with body fluids through splattering and mouth-to-mouth resuscitation; ·Unprotected handling of infected carcass; ·Ingestion of raw infected meat; ·Exposure to bats; ·All Category II exposures on head and neck area. 

**Reference:** National Rabies Prevention and Control Program, Manual of Procedures. 2019. https://doh.gov.ph/sites/default/files/publications/Rabies%20Manual_MOP_2019%20nov28.pdf

Assumptions about the mean and standard deviation can be made

rationale.text:
NONparametric tests are used for ordinal and nominal data, not parametric. Parametric tests are used to analyze continuous variables (ratio and interval data). Parametric tests can be used when the following assumptions are met: Normally distributed sample; ·Sample is randomly selected; Homogenous variances if 2-or more groups are sampled. If these assumptions are not met, non-parametric test can be used.

question: In a case-control study investigating the association of smoking with COPD, controls are deliberately selected from a hospital population rather than from the community. What type of bias is illustrated from the case above?

rationale.text:
This illustrates selection bias. In this case, controls chosen from the hospital is not representative of the prevalence of smoking in the community where COPD cases arise. The association of the exposure to the disease is weakened by the selection of hospital controls because smoking causes many diseases resulting in hospitalization, thereby leading to selection bias. Other examples of selection bias: ·An example is convenience sampling wherein patients are assigned based on ease of contact (as in the case question); ·Attrition bias: participants lost to follow up; ·Berkson bias: cases and/or controls selected from hospitals. 

**Reference:** Le, T., Bhushan, V., & Sochat, M. (2023). First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2022, Thirty Third Edition (33rd ed., p. 262). McGraw-Hill Education.

question: What type of bias is being exhibited by the Hawthorne effect wherein participants adjust their behavior because they are aware that they are being observed?

rationale.text:
Measurement bias occurs when the data is gathered in a non-systematic way. Examples of measurement bias include: ·Using faulty measuring equipment; ·Hawthorne effect: subjects adjust their behavior upon being aware that they are being observed. Procedure bias occurs when the study participants in the treatment and non-treatment group are not treated the same. Observer-expectancy bias is influenced by the investigator's belief in the efficacy of the treatment which results in the alteration of the outcome (also called Pygmalion effect). Selection bias occurs when the sampling or intervention allocation is not random resulting to a nonrepresentative sample. 

**Reference:** Le, T., Bhushan, V., & Sochat, M. (2023). First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2022, Thirty Third Edition (33rd ed., p. 262). McGraw-Hill Education.

rationale.text:
Perinatal mortality rate is the number of infant deaths under age 7 days and fetal deaths at 28 weeks gestation or more per 1,000 live births and fetal deaths at 28 weeks of gestation or more. question: In an epidemic, the pathogen is transmitted through person-to-person contact, as a result, the number of cases increases over time. What epidemic pattern is described?

rationale.text:
A propagated outbreak results from transmission from one person to another. Usually, transmission is by direct person-to-person contact, as with syphilis. Transmission may also be vehicleborne (e.g., transmission of hepatitis B or HIV by sharing needles) or vectorborne (e.g., transmission of yellow fever by mosquitoes). In a continuous common-source outbreak, the range of exposures and range of incubation periods tend to flatten and widen the peaks of the epidemic curve. The epidemic curve of an intermittent common-source outbreak often has a pattern reflecting the intermittent nature of the exposure. If the group is exposed over a relatively brief period, so that everyone who becomes ill does so within one incubation period, then the common-source outbreak is further classified as a point-source outbreak.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: It is considered as the simplest form of probability sampling:

rationale.text:
Simple random sampling is the simplest form of probability sampling. In this type of sampling there is an equal probability that each eligible member of the target population will be chosen for the study. A sample of people from this population is chosen at random for the study or survey. Convenience sampling is not a type of probability sampling because it is based on ease of contact. A list of the primary clusters is necessary for one-stage sampling. In a cluster sample, smaller sampling units known as observation units are combined into larger sampling units known as clusters. 

**Reference:** Guidance, examples and tools for probability sampling when designing a population-based biomonitoring study (n.d.). Retrieved February 27, 2023, from https://www.cdc.gov/nceh/tracking/pdfs/BiomonitoringStudyGuidance-508.pdf

question: Using volunteers as subjects for a research is an example of what type of sampling?

rationale.text:
Convenience sampling occurs when patients are assigned based on ease of contact. Using volunteers as study participants is an example of this.
